item.title: Araghchi French FM discuss Iran-France ties regional and international developments
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who is in New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, met and held talks with French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot on Tuesday afternoon on the sidelines of the session. The two sides discussed and exchanged views on developments related to Iran-France diplomatic relations, as well as regional and international developments. Iran’s Foreign Minister criticized France’s interventionist positions toward Iran and stressed the need for the French Embassy to respect Iran’s domestic laws and regulations. The Foreign Minister also described France’s positions on regional developments, particularly regarding the US and Israeli military aggression against Iran, as unacceptable. Referring to France’s double standards regarding human rights, he noted that France cannot claim to care about human rights while remaining silent in the face of the US and Israeli crimes against humanity against the Iranian people and the killing of Iranian women and children, and while cooperating in the implementation of the US’s illegal sanctions against the Iranian people. Araghchi stressed that the Islamic Republic of Iran seeks relations based on mutual respect and mutual interests with all countries, including France, but will act seriously and decisively in defending its interests and national objectives.

The foreign ministers of Iran and Iraq described safeguarding the security of their shared border as highly important and stressed the importance of implementing the agreements reached in this regard and effectively confronting terrorist activities. item.title: Iranian Austrian Foreign Ministers discuss regional international developments
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and Austrian Foreign Minister Beate Meinl-Reisinger held talks on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. The two sides discussed and exchanged views on the most important international and regional developments, as well as bilateral issues of mutual interest. The Iranian foreign minister, explaining the ongoing developments in the region, said the insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz and disruption to shipping are a direct result of the aggressive actions of the United States and the Israeli regime. He stressed that restoring the security of shipping in the region requires an end to the destabilizing actions and economic terrorism of the United States. The foreign minister also pointed to the continuation of the genocide against Palestinians and the Israeli regime’s flagrant violations of international law, as well as the regime’s continued aggression against Lebanon and other countries in the region. He stressed the responsibility of all countries, particularly European countries, to halt any support for the occupying regime and end its impunity.

item.title: Iranian FM Araghchi meets Greek counterpart in New York
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who has traveled to New York to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, met and held talks with Georgios Gerapetritis, Foreign Minister of Greece, at noon on Tuesday. During the meeting, the latest state of Iran-Greece bilateral relations, interactions between Iran and the European Union, and the latest regional and international developments were discussed and views were exchanged. Referring to the longstanding and historic relations between the two countries, the Iranian Foreign Minister stressed the importance of continuing political consultations and developing economic and cultural cooperation between Tehran and Athens. Araghchi also elaborated on the Islamic Republic of Iran’s positions regarding developments in West Asia, stressing the need for all countries to abide by international law, safeguard national sovereignty, and respect the UN Charter. He noted that countering unilateralism and acts of aggression is the primary condition for maintaining international stability and security. The Greek Foreign Minister, for his part, welcomed the continuation of bilateral dialogue and stressed his country’s interest in strengthening the path of diplomacy and playing a constructive role in resolving regional and international disputes.

item.title: Araghchi Meets with Belarusian Foreign Minister in New York
item.description: Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran, met and held talks with Maxim Ryzhenkov, Foreign Minister of Belarus, as part of his bilateral meetings on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. During the meeting, the latest state of Iran-Belarus bilateral relations, ways to expand economic and trade cooperation, and the latest regional and international developments were reviewed. Referring to the excellent and growing relations between the two countries, the Iranian Foreign Minister stressed the Islamic Republic of Iran’s determination to fully implement previous agreements and deepen cooperation in bilateral and multilateral fields. Araghchi strongly criticized the unilateral and illegal sanctions imposed by the West on independent countries and stressed the need for Iran and Belarus to create synergies and jointly stand firm against political and economic pressures stemming from the sources of unilateralism. The Belarusian Foreign Minister, for his part, expressed satisfaction with the meeting and stressed Minsk’s firm determination to strengthen fraternal and strategic relations with Tehran, describing safeguarding the UN Charter and the national sovereignty of countries as a fundamental principle in international interactions.

Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who has traveled to New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, met with Antonio Tajani, Foreign Minister of Italy, on Tuesday morning. During the meeting, the two sides discussed and exchanged views on Iran-Italy bilateral relations as well as regional and international developments. The Iranian Foreign Minister explained the Islamic Republic of Iran’s views on international developments, warning of the dangerous consequences of the normalization of lawlessness and the United States’ aggressive unilateralism for the rule of law. He stressed the importance of all countries, particularly European countries, fulfilling their international legal obligations in this regard. Araghchi described the hosting of US military bases by some European countries, including Italy, and any cooperation in preparing for or carrying out acts of aggression against Iran as highly dangerous and qtantamount to complicity in aggression, saying that such actions entail international responsibility for the host or complicit states. Referring to the continuation of aggressive and destabilizing actions by the United States and the Israeli regime in West Asia, the Iranian Foreign Minister noted that the increase in fuel and commodity prices in global markets is a direct result of the US-Israeli military aggression against Iran, adding that any responsible country should hold the United States accountable for continuing its adventurist actions and threatening commercial shipping in the Persian Gulf region and the Strait of Hormuz. The Foreign Minister, elaborating on Iran’s responsible approach to regional developments, including its participation in diplomatic processes that were at one point hosted by Italy, recalled the fact that the United States committed military aggression against Iran in the midst of diplomatic negotiations, destroying the diplomatic processes, and regrettably, European countries, instead of condemning the aggression, adopted a policy of appeasement toward the aggressor. Araghchi stressed that Iran regards diplomacy as an effective tool for defending its national sovereignty and legitimate interests, and that just as it has acted decisively in repelling acts of aggression, it has also remained committed to and acted in good faith in using the instrument of diplomacy. Regarding human rights, particularly women’s rights, the Foreign Minister criticized the double standards of some European countries, stating that those who remained silent in the face of the most blatant violations of human rights by the Israeli occupying regime in occupied Palestine, remained indifferent to the US and Israeli crimes against the Iranian people, including in Minab and Lamerd, and are now supporting US economic terrorism against the Iranian people have no standing to lecture others on human rights. The Italian Foreign Minister, for his part, stressed Italy’s commitment to international peace and security and called for redoubled efforts by all parties to reduce tensions.

Seyed Abbas Araghchi, Foreign Minister of the Islamic Republic of Iran, who has traveled to New York to attend the annual session of the United Nations General Assembly, met and held talks with Ignazio Cassis, Foreign Minister of Switzerland, on the sidelines of the session on Tuesday morning. The two sides discussed and exchanged views on Iran-Switzerland bilateral relations as well as regional and international developments. The Iranian Foreign Minister explained the positions of the Islamic Republic of Iran regarding regional developments following the US-Israeli acts of aggression against Iran and the continuation of interventionist actions, the maritime blockade and economic warfare against the Iranian people. He underscored the responsibility of all countries to safeguard the UN Charter and international law, particularly the principle prohibiting the use of force. Referring to the war crimes committed by the United States and Israel against Iran during their military aggression over the past year and a half, he stressed the Islamic Republic of Iran’s determination to resolutely defend its security and national sovereignty. Referring to the repeated breaches of commitments by the United States, including its violation of the Islamabad Understanding and the escalation of its acts of aggression against Iran, Araghchi recalled the responsibility of the international community to hold the United States accountable for the consequences of its unlawful actions. Araghchi also referred to the gross violations of international humanitarian law by the United States and the Israeli regime and the commission of numerous war crimes, including the Minab and Lamerd tragedies. He underscored the duty of all states parties to the 1949 Geneva Conventions to pursue and punish the perpetrators in accordance with the fundamental rule of “respect for and ensuring respect for international humanitarian law.” He warned that indifference toward genocide and war crimes, as well as the continued impunity of perpetrators, would have far-reaching consequences for the entire world and all countries. The two sides also discussed and exchanged views on Iran-Switzerland cooperation aimed at helping strengthen peace and stability in the region.
